To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

cyclopentenonyl oxylipins are potent signals that activate detoxification, defense, and secondary metabolism in plants, a response mediated by the transcription factors TGA5 and TGA2, and that this signaling pathway is activated by a wide range of lipid peroxidation–derived electrophiles, which may be sensed as xenobiotics.

oxidized lipids are potent inducers of detoxification and stress responses, that the induction profile is similar to that of a broad-spectrum detoxifying response, and that the induction is dependent on TGA transcription factors.
oxidized fatty acids induce the expression of detoxification and stress responses genes through the TGA transcription factor pathway.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the biological activity of oxidized lipids, a group of signaling molecules that are formed in plants during normal growth and development and during stress.
the role of oxidized fatty acids as signaling molecules in plant responses to environmental stresses.
the identification, biosynthesis, and biological activity of phytoprostanes, the most abundant group of cyclopentene fatty acid oxidation products in plants.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
cyclopentenonic oxylipins are a novel class of signaling molecules in plants that induce detoxification and stress responses.
the cyclopentenonyl oxylipins are potent signals that induce the expression of detoxification genes, and they are also reactive electrophiles and thus potential protein-damaging agents.

cyclopentenonic oxylipins, such as phytoprostanes, 12-oxoplinolenic acid, and 12-epoxy-12,13-dihydroxy-9Z-octadecenoic acid (12S-HpODE), are potent inducers of a broad-spectrum detoxication network in Arabidopsis thaliana that is mediated by the TGA transcription factor family.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
oxidized lipids are not only potent signals, but also potent electrophiles, and that the TGA transcription factor network is the major target of both properties.
the plant hormone jasmonic acid is a cyclopentanonic derivative, whereas the cyclopentenonic derivatives are stress signals.
oxidized fatty acid metabolites are not only important signals in the regulation of plant defense, but also act as general stress signals and detoxifying agents.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the cyclopentenonic oxylipin phytoprostanes, which are formed by free radical–catabolism of lipids, are potent signals that induce a defense program similar to that induced by jasmonic acid and other xenobiotic lipids.
oxidized lipids can be considered as a new class of plant hormones.

oxidized lipids, such as phytoprostanes, are important regulators of plant growth and defense responses and that the TGA transcription factor network is involved in mediating the effects of oxidized lipids on plant development.
